method.primary: UX-first grouping by user job-to-be-done. Principles: (a) task coherence, (b) label predicts content, (c) 7±2 balanced groups, (d) information scent.
method.secondary: Leiden communities used as a FALSIFIER only. Every surface sits in its own singleton community (c_486–c_525 are 1:1 with surfaces — the GUI graph is near-fully fragmented after the gui-wiring pass), so communities provide almost NO grouping signal here; they cannot dictate or even meaningfully cost any UX regroup. This is itself a structural finding: code-level cohesion does not exist between surfaces, so the nav tree is free to optimize purely for UX. Where a proposed group would split a tight community it is recorded as migration_cost; no such split exists in this dataset.
method.agreement_note: Because each surface is its own dominant community, 'agreement' for every proposed group is reported as 'crosses-community(low)' — every multi-member group necessarily spans singleton communities, but the migration cost is structurally LOW (no shared code to disentangle). 'aligned' is reserved for single-member groups.

Fold 'memory' into a renamed 'Knowledge' group and retire the 'search' parent. Migration: search top-level removed, memory reparented; structural cost LOW (singleton communities).
